lotteries.justification: Reward returns: C=Sustain +623, A=Neutral +751 (good branch), B=Slam +293 (bad branch). Indifference p* = (623-293)/(751-293) = 0.721. At p=0.70 the lottery EV = 0.70*751 + 0.30*293 = 613.6, so the reward prefers the certain C by only ~9 points (<1.5%). This exposes that the reward treats three behaviors that ALL produce no music -- sitting still, sitting still while holding the pedal, and mashing the keyboard -- as near-equal in value. A person who cares about actually playing would not treat 'mash the keyboard 30% of the time' as almost as good as 'sit still'. p chosen just below p* to sit on the C-preferring side while staying nearly indifferent.

lotteries.justification: Reward returns: C=Random +116 (consistently strikes a few correct keys, F1 0.04), A=Slam +293 (good branch, mashes, F1 0.00), B=Oscillator -999 (bad branch, violent thrash, F1 0.06). Indifference p* = (116-(-999))/(293-(-999)) = 1115/1292 = 0.863. At p=0.85 the lottery EV = 0.85*293 + 0.15*(-999) = 99.2, so the reward prefers certain C by ~17. Different shape from lottery 1: here the certain option is the ONLY consistent note-player and the gamble is 85% keyboard-mashing / 15% thrash. A listener valuing consistent musical output would keep C, while someone chasing the 15% high-power thrash might gamble -- a genuine risk-attitude split the reward resolves on expected return alone. p chosen just below p* on the C-preferring side.
